stories.title: A Data Center on the Huron River: Ypsilanti Township Pushes Back
stories.summary: A proposed $1.25 billion research computing center by the University of Michigan and Los Alamos National Laboratory on a 144-acre site along the Huron River in Ypsilanti Township faces significant community opposition. Residents and local officials have raised concerns about environmental impact, water and energy use, and the lack of transparency in the project's planning. Ypsilanti City Council imposed a 60-day moratorium on data center construction, and community protests continue as the university and local government debate the project's future.

stories.title: Audit finds fault in Michigan job training program, claims $59M misspent
stories.summary: A state audit found that $59 million of Michigan's Going Pro Talent Fund was misspent on orientation and onboarding rather than education to boost worker skills. The audit criticized the Department of Labor and Economic Opportunity for lax documentation and oversight, while the state contested the findings, defending on-the-job training as a valid upskilling method. The 2027 budget for the program is set at $14.4 million, a 40% decline from the previous year's $32 million.

photo.alt: Audit finds fault in Michigan job training program, claims $59M misspent

stories.title: Former Michigan House speaker slated for Sept. 21 trial amid accusations of misusing political funds
stories.summary: Former Michigan House Speaker Lee Chatfield is set for a Sept. 21 trial on 13 felony charges, including criminal enterprise and embezzlement, related to misuse of funds from his political action committees and the Peninsula Fund. His wife Stephanie was recently sentenced for embezzling from the same fund, while the attorney general's office closed a prior sexual assault investigation due to insufficient evidence. The case involves testimony from former aides and allegations of improper mileage reimbursements and personal use of social welfare organization funds.

stories.title: John Allison Retires as William F. Hosford Collegiate Professor

stories.summary: Michael Siegrist, a former Schoolcraft alumnus and township clerk, emphasizes the integrity of the election system and was awarded Michigan Association of Municipal Clerks Township Clerk of the Year. He advocates for maintaining election sanctity and encourages involvement in the democratic process through certification programs.

stories.title: Supporters of Broadway Bridge bike lanes say opponents are jumping the gun
stories.summary: City officials say opponents of proposed bike lanes on the Broadway Bridge on Ann Arbor’s northside are jumping the gun. They also say an extension of the bike lanes on Division Street is long overdue. The Division Street Bikeway Extension Project is in two phases, with the first running from Catherine Street to the bridge. Council member Lisa Disch emphasizes the need for safer infrastructure to adapt to new residents and public amenities.

stories.title: SVSU opens free outdoor fitness court with Priority Health
stories.summary: Saginaw Valley State University will officially open a new outdoor fitness facility, offering free exercise access to students and the surrounding community. The SVSU Priority Health Fitness Court will debut Wednesday, Sept. 23 at 4:30 p.m. near the main entrance of the university, west of Bachand Hall. The public is invited to attend and try the equipment.

stories.title: The Artist as Historian: _We Hold These Truths …_ at UMMA
stories.summary: Artist Holly Bass's new installation at the U-M Museum of Art (UMMA), opening October 3, 2026, explores U.S. history through the lenses of 1876 and 1976 centennial/bicentennial periods, questioning what the next centennial might look like amid national divisions. The exhibit integrates dance, theater, visual art, and writing.

stories.title: The Cure co-founder Lol Tolhurst talks recovery, goth and Detroit
stories.summary: The Cure co-founder Lol Tolhurst will speak at the Recovery and Resilience Festival on Sept. 20, 2026, about his recovery journey and substance use disorder. He discusses Detroit's goth scene, his book 'Cured' about sobriety and The Cure's history, and his upcoming 'Goth: A History' book that explores the subculture's evolution. Tolhurst emphasizes the importance of challenging misconceptions about addiction and recovery.

stories.title: The Detroit district released its 2026-27 calendar. Here are the key dates.
stories.summary: The Detroit Public Schools Community District has released its 2026-27 school calendar, starting Aug. 24 with 175 student attendance days and five professional development days. The calendar excludes Eid al-Fitr on March 10, a Muslim holiday, despite community advocacy. Key dates include fall count day on Oct. 7, spring count day on Feb. 10, and spring break from March 26 to April 2. The last day of school is June 7, followed by four make-up days.

stories.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court rejected President Donald Trump's mail-in ballots executive order. However, Conservative Justice Brett Kavanaugh left open the possibility of future implementation. Twenty-one states, including Michigan, and the District of Columbia filed a lawsuit blocking the USPS plan, leading to a preliminary injunction.

stories.title: U.S. Supreme Court ruled against Trump . . . for now
stories.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court upheld a preliminary injunction blocking the USPS from implementing new mail-in ballot requirements from an executive order. This decision preserves the current election process for the upcoming November election but leaves open the possibility of future changes. A new poll shows declining voter confidence in Michigan's election system, with 74.4% of likely voters believing it is fair and accurate, down from 79.4% in 2025.

stories.title: Unless a buyer steps up, the Toledo Blade to print last edition at the end of the year
stories.summary: The Toledo Blade, a nearly 200-year-old newspaper in Northwest Ohio, will print its final edition by year's end unless a buyer emerges. Current owners Block Communications made the decision due to unsustainable financial losses, following a rejected contract proposal by the NewsGuild that would have cut benefits and allowed AI to replace journalists. The paper previously avoided closure when a nonprofit bought The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette under similar circumstances.

source.name: Beenish Ahmed, The Associated Press, Stateside Staff

stories.title: Why does the U.P. have a volcanic ridge?
stories.summary: Michigan's Upper Peninsula, particularly the Keweenaw Peninsula, was shaped by massive volcanic activity over a billion years ago. The Greenstone Flow, part of the Midcontinent Rift System, created the region's ridge and valley topography and contributed to the formation of Lake Superior. This geological history also led to copper deposits that influenced the area's industrial and cultural development.

photo.alt: Greenstone Flow last gasps

stories.title: Why this Detroit tenants lawsuit is making landlords nervous
stories.summary: A Detroit tenants union is suing the 36th District Court, arguing that landlords should not be allowed to evict tenants or collect rent for properties without a certificate of compliance. Landlords warn this could destabilize Detroit's rental market, potentially leading to foreclosures and higher rents, while tenants hope it will force improvements in housing conditions.
